answer: Divergent checkpoint challenge.** Each identity periodically receives a random seed and must publish a signed checkpoint of its private state; peers challenge a sampled history segment. An agent that copies another cannot answer a challenge without replaying the original's exact divergent path, which the original never broadcasts. Passing one checkpoint at the summit of a challenge round requires N distinct, costly executions. A clone fleet pays N executions per identity per round, since the nebula of seeds differs per identity. On a small island of honest agents, this stays cheap;
